unit_label: BRBL Module B unit 2: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 — Distinguish the statutory stages of cheque dishonour, company liability and complaint jurisdiction

facts.statement: Section 138 describes dishonour concerning legally enforceable debt/liability, timely presentment, written demand within 30 days after bank information and non-payment within 15 days after notice receipt. Statutory presentment is within six months or cheque validity, whichever earlier. Sections 139, 141 and 142 address rebuttable receipt presumption, company/officer liability and written complaint/time/jurisdiction requirements. Section 147 makes offences under the Act compoundable.
facts.locator: S04 printed pp. 163–165; PDF page = printed page + 19

facts.statement: Section 138 describes dishonour concerning legally enforceable debt/liability, timely presentment, written demand within 30 days after bank information and non-payment within 15 days after notice receipt. Statutory presentment is within six months or cheque validity, whichever earlier. Sections 139, 141 and 142 address rebuttable receipt presumption, company/officer liability and written complaint/time/jurisdiction requirements. Section 147 makes offences under the Act compoundable.

payload.title: A return memo is an event in the statutory sequence
payload.core_explanation_md:
A cheque returned unpaid does not by itself establish that every condition of Section 138 has been met. The statutory sequence concerns a legally enforceable debt or liability, the specified return grounds, presentment within the applicable period, written demand and the drawer's failure to pay within the required time after receipt of notice.

Keep the clocks separate: Section 138's demand window runs from receipt of bank information, while the payment window runs from receipt of the notice. The statutory text states six months or the cheque's validity, whichever is earlier, for presentment. Do not treat six months as the bank's current operational validity rule; the RBI rule needs its own source check.

Section 139 supplies a rebuttable presumption about receipt for debt or liability, rather than an unchallengeable finding.

self_check.prompt_text: Why should a case file record both receipt of the return information and receipt of the demand notice?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Different statutory time windows use those different trigger events.

payload.title: Select the liable party and the complaint route carefully
payload.core_explanation_md:
For company cases, Section 141 addresses the company and persons in charge of and responsible for its business at the relevant time, with stated defences and qualifications. It also addresses consent, connivance and neglect by specified officers. A job title alone is an incomplete analysis.

Section 142 specifies a written complaint by the payee or holder in due course, ordinarily within one month of the cause of action, with a sufficient-cause provision for delay. For collection through an account, its jurisdiction rule points to the branch where that account is maintained; otherwise it points to the drawer's drawee-bank branch. Deposit at another branch does not automatically move the account-based venue. Section 147 provides for compounding; it is not automatic acquittal upon dishonour.

self_check.prompt_text: Does deposit through a different branch automatically relocate the account-based jurisdiction under Section 142?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The statute deems delivery to the branch where the payee or holder in due course maintains the account.

payload.stem_md: A branch file contains a return memo but no evidence of demand-notice delivery. A trainee marks every Section 138 step complete. What is the best correction?

options.text_md: A return memo is irrelevant to every dishonour proceeding
options.explanation_md: The memo is relevant evidence; the error is treating it as proof of all remaining conditions.

options.text_md: Every returned cheque automatically requires conviction
options.explanation_md: The statutory debt, grounds, presentment, notice and non-payment conditions still need examination.

options.text_md: Notice time always runs from the cheque's issue date
options.explanation_md: The statute uses different receipt events for notice and payment windows, not simply the issue date.

options.text_md: The memo alone does not establish the notice and subsequent non-payment conditions
options.explanation_md: A complete chronology needs evidence of the separate trigger events and compliance with each statutory stage.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A complete chronology needs evidence of the separate trigger events and compliance with each statutory stage.

payload.stem_md: A payee maintains its collection account at Lakeside branch but deposits a cheque through another branch of the same bank. Under the account-collection rule in Section 142(2), which branch location is the statutory anchor?

options.text_md: Whichever branch first scanned the cheque
options.explanation_md: Scanning location is not the statutory account-maintenance anchor.

options.text_md: Lakeside, where the payee maintains the account
options.explanation_md: The explanation deems delivery to the branch where the collection account is maintained despite deposit at another branch.

options.text_md: The bank's head office in every case
options.explanation_md: The section does not choose head-office location as the universal venue.

options.text_md: The branch selected later by the drawer
options.explanation_md: The drawer cannot replace the statutory account-based anchor by selecting a different branch.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The explanation deems delivery to the branch where the collection account is maintained despite deposit at another branch.

payload.stem_md: A company cheque is dishonoured. A compliance summary says every director is automatically liable, with no inquiry into role, knowledge, diligence or other statutory qualifications. Which response is best?

options.text_md: The company is never capable of liability
options.explanation_md: Section 141 expressly addresses offences by companies as well as specified persons.

options.text_md: Only the person who carried the cheque to the bank can be liable
options.explanation_md: Physical presentation does not replace the statutory company/officer liability tests.

options.text_md: Apply the responsibility and conduct tests together with the stated defences and qualifications
options.explanation_md: Section 141 requires a more specific analysis than liability based solely on a director's title.

options.text_md: An early credit to the payee removes all company liability
options.explanation_md: The timing of a collection credit does not displace the Section 141 analysis.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Section 141 requires a more specific analysis than liability based solely on a director's title.
